intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: In 2015 a traditional stone-laying ceremony was held on Cerro Pachón, in Chile, to commemorate the official start of construction.

intervals.label: operations
intervals.note: Sources disagree on the month: the Rubin survey-strategy page says "as of June 29, 2026"; the Rubin LSST page says "in June 2026"; the Rubin About page says "in July 2026"; the DOE Office of Science announcement is dated 30 June 2026. 29 June 2026 is used (the only day-precision statement from a Rubin page).
intervals.quote: Rubin Observatory has begun the 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) as of June 29, 2026.

name: Simonyi Survey Telescope and LSST Camera
notes: The detector operations interval starts at the LSST survey start; the commissioning interval is recorded on the experiment.

placements.note: Start is the month the LSST Camera was installed on the telescope; the telescope structure and mirrors reached the summit in 2018.
placements.quote: In March 2025, the LSST Camera — the largest digital camera in the world — was installed on the telescope

diameter.note: Diameter of the primary mirror (M1), which is a combined primary/tertiary surface.

summary.plain: An 8.4-metre telescope with a very short, wide view and a 3.2-gigapixel camera, built to photograph the entire visible southern sky every few nights.
summary.technical: Simonyi Survey Telescope (8.4 m combined primary/tertiary, 3.42 m secondary, 3.5-degree field) with the 3.2-gigapixel LSST Camera (64 cm focal plane).

technology.quote: 3.5-degree field of view covering a 64 cm diameter flat focal plane
technology.value: 8.4 m reflecting survey telescope with a 3.5-degree field of view covering a 64 cm diameter flat focal plane, carrying the 3.2-gigapixel LSST Camera.
